prompt: Explain inflation using only tailgating metaphors. Do not stop when the metaphors break down.
response:
Inflation is when the whole parking lot starts “tailgating” harder.

At first, everyone brings normal supplies: burgers, buns, charcoal, chips, cooler ice, team flags. A burger costs one high-five, a soda costs two fist bumps, and a parking spot costs the usual “my cousin knows a guy” amount.

Then suddenly, there are way more fans trying to party in the same lot, or everyone shows up with extra coolers full of high-fives to spend. Now the guy with the grill realizes people are waving more high-fives at him than he has burgers. So he says, “Burgers are now three high-fives.” The soda table sees this and says, “Sodas are now four fist bumps.” The parking attendant says, “That patch of asphalt near the porta-potties is premium real estate.”

That’s inflation: the tailgate bucks don’t stretch as far. Same cooler, fewer wings.

Sometimes it happens because there’s too much “tailgate cash” sloshing around the lot. Everybody has extra wristbands, drink tickets, and ceremonial foam fingers to trade, but the number of hot dogs hasn’t increased. When more fans chase the same number of hot dogs, the hot dogs start acting like VIP brisket.

Sometimes it happens because supplies get harder to bring in. Maybe the highway to the stadium is jammed, the propane truck is late, the nacho cheese pipeline kinks, or the guy who always brings the folding tables stayed home. Now even if the crowd is the same size, the lot has fewer usable snacks, fewer grills, fewer chairs. So the price of everything rises because the tailgate is short on essentials.

Wages are like promising your buddy more ribs to keep him flipping burgers. If the grillmaster says, “I’m not standing in smoke for three quarters unless I get more ribs,” then the host gives him more ribs. But now the host needs to charge more high-fives per burger to cover the rib raise. Then the cooler captain wants more ribs too. Then the playlist guy wants craft ribs.
